resolution.locator: BACKGAMMON / Bearing off the Men / p. 276
resolution.quote: If the winner has borne off all his men before his adversary has begun to do the same, the game is known as a "gammon." resolution.reason: The blind question has two parts. The gap (a loser who began bearing off, was hit, and has a man outside his home table but neither up nor in the winner's home table) is the reference's game-value question. The overlap is not: a loser who has borne off nothing and has a man up satisfies both 'before his adversary has begun to do the same' and 'a man or men up', and the corpus does not say which result he suffers. The reference's note admitted that 'an ordering had to be chosen, backgammon first, and clear does not record that a choice was made', which is an implementer's reading chosen silently. Fixed: game-value's question states the overlap as well as the gap; the note's sentence about it is removed.
